name: Eat like a bodybuilder (rice/chicken/broccoli)

lead: Chicken, rice and broccoli is the traditional bodybuilding plate, eaten in planned portions to build muscle or lose fat. The payoff is a more muscular, leaner physique with very few daily food decisions.

The chain is high protein plus measured carbohydrate, which makes calorie intake easy to control: a surplus with enough protein supports muscle gain alongside training, and a deficit supports fat loss. The three-food menu itself hasn't been trialled, but calorie balance and protein intake are widely covered in sports nutrition.

paras: People cook large batches and repeat the same meals across bulking phases (eating above maintenance) and cutting phases (eating below it), adjusting portions of rice and protein. Competitive bodybuilders start cutting roughly 12 to 14 weeks before a contest, and visible changes build over weeks to months alongside lifting.

Risks depend on the amounts and on extreme contest-prep methods such as dehydration. Very repetitive menus can limit variety and be hard to sustain, and individual needs differ, so people with medical conditions or a history of disordered eating may want professional guidance.

angle.text: The rice, chicken and broccoli template is used to gain muscle or cut fat with very few food decisions, building a leaner, more muscular physique. High protein and measured carbs make calorie control easy, and calorie control plus training is what changes body composition. The principles are well studied in sports nutrition; the three-food menu is a convention.

lead: Eating like a bodybuilder, often shorthand for plain rice, chicken breast and broccoli, is a long-standing fitness diet built around high protein, measured carbohydrate and low added fat. It is used in appearance communities to gain muscle or lose fat while keeping food choices simple.

Wikipedia describes competitive bodybuilders alternating between bulking, a calorie surplus to build muscle, and cutting, a deficit begun about 12 to 14 weeks before a contest [1]. Typical foods include chicken, turkey, beef, fish, eggs, dairy and slow-digesting carbohydrates [1].
No clinical trial has tested the specific rice, chicken and broccoli meal pattern as such; the underlying principles of calorie balance and protein intake are discussed in sports nutrition.

paras: Bulking means eating in a calorie surplus and cutting means a deficit meant to lose fat while keeping muscle; larger surpluses tend to add more fat, and larger deficits raise the risk of muscle loss [1]. Clean bulking aims for little fat gain, while dirty bulking uses a large surplus often from junk food [1].

Experts disagree on protein targets, with views ranging from about 1 g per pound of body weight per day to 1.5 to 2 g or more [1]. Many bodybuilders eat five to seven meals daily, though Wikipedia notes studies show no metabolic advantage over three meals a day [1]. Contest preparation often adds cardio and, in the last stage, carbohydrate loading and dehydration [1].

timeline.event: Nutrition for bulking and cutting, protein and supplements became part of bodybuilding culture [1].
